intent: Compare the relative us-versus-them polarization trends in the Senate and House of Representatives across the congressional periods shown, and identify when each chamber reaches its highest level.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
What is the Senate relative us-versus-them polarization trajectory across the congressional periods shown?
Identify when each chamber reaches its highest level of relative polarization.
How do the Senate and House trajectories compare over the periods where both have data?
At what plotted value and position does each chamber reach its highest relative polarization?

units.claim: All 2 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: In the Senate, relative us-versus-them polarization falls from 0.9179 in 1973-74 to 0.2800 in 1985-86, then rises to 1.0000 by 2009-10.
units.computation: 1973-74=0.9179; 1985-86=0.2800; 2009-10=1.0000. The series therefore declines substantially before rising to its maximum.
accept: Senate polarization declines substantially between 1973-74 and 1985-86.
Senate polarization then rises to 1.0000 by 2009-10.
reject: Describes the Senate series as generally rising from the start with only a small dip.
Describes the Senate series as declining overall.

units.claim: In the House of Representatives, relative us-versus-them polarization rises from the 1979-80 period to the 2003-04 period.
units.computation: Compare first (0.0100) and last (0.8058) values for the House series.
accept: House polarization is higher at the end than at the start
reject: House polarization is flat across periods

units.claim: Between 1979-80 and 2003-04, both chamber series end higher than they start, but the House generally rises while the Senate first falls to 0.2708 at point_order 14 and then rises sharply.
units.computation: Over the overlap, Senate moves from 0.3979 at 1979-80 to 0.9800 at 2003-04, with an intervening minimum of 0.2708 at point_order 14. House moves from 0.0100 at 1979-80 to 0.8058 at 2003-04.
accept: Both chambers end the overlap higher than they start.
The Senate first declines and then rises sharply, while the House generally rises over the overlap.
reject: Claims both series rise monotonically over the overlap.
Claims the two series end lower than they start.

units.claim: The Senate reaches 1.0000 at 2009-10. The House reaches its plotted maximum of 0.8122 at point_order 38, between the 1997-98 and 2003-04 anchors; the explicit 2003-04 value is 0.8058.
units.computation: Senate max=1.0000 at 2009-10. House max=0.8122 at point_order 38, which is between the labeled 1997-98 anchor at point_order 33 and the labeled 2003-04 anchor at point_order 43; the 2003-04 value is 0.8058.
accept: House maximum is 0.8122 at point_order 38, between 1997-98 and 2003-04.
The explicit 2003-04 House value is 0.8058 and is not the plotted maximum.
reject: Claims the House maximum is 0.8058 at 2003-04.
Claims the Senate maximum occurs at 1973-74.

unsupported_to_avoid: Claims about periods where a chamber has no data
Exact percentage changes not directly computed from the table
review_notes: The Senate series has an unlabeled minimum row at point_order 14 (0.2708); it is not used as an x-anchored basis row.
The House series has an unlabeled maximum row at point_order 38 (0.8122); the labeled 2003-04 value 0.8058 is used for the peak claim to keep x explicit.
Closure truth correction 2026-10-29: claims, ranges, computations, and relations were checked against data_table.csv.
